headline: Learned models recover biological quantities from sparse, noisy, or indirect omics data
label: Machine Learning For Omics Analysis
summary: Single-cell references, self-supervised upscaling, and nanopore segmentation now yield deconvolution and methylation estimates from limited assays.
synthesis: The common thread is learned inference that recovers biologically meaningful quantities from limited or indirectly measured data. cellGeometry applies non-negative geometric deconvolution to estimate cell-type proportions from bulk RNA-seq using single-cell references. omnideconv provides a unifying framework that benchmarks second-generation single-cell-informed deconvolution methods on accuracy, scalability, and robustness. ARUNA, a self-supervised denoising convolutional autoencoder, imputes genome-wide CpG methylation from sparse RRBS data toward WGBS resolution. Campolina applies convolutional segmentation to raw nanopore signals and is reported to outperform Scrappie on R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 data. What is new is reference-guided or self-supervised inference that upscales constrained assays, paired with systematic benchmarking of existing deconvolution tools. The nanopore and methylation items address upstream measurement quality, whereas the deconvolution pair addresses bulk-to-single-cell inference.
